question_en: Which of the following statements about hypothesis testing is most accurate?
option_a: The probability of a Type I error is equal to the significance level of the test.
option_b: The power of a test is one minus the probability of a Type I error.
option_c: If you can disprove the null hypothesis, then you have proven the alternative hypothesis.
explanation_en: The probability of getting a test statistic outside the critical value(s) when the null is true is the level of significance and is the probability of a Type I error. The power of a test is 1 minus the probability of a Type II error. Hypothesis testing does not prove a hypothesis, we either reject the null or fail to reject it.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Quantitative Method\Reading 8 Hypothesis Testing - Answers.pdf
question_en: A data analyst compares the P/E ratios for two companies over a period of 20 years and calculates a two-tailed F-statistic that exceeds the critical F-statistic value. As a result of her findings, she will:
option_a: not reject the null hypothesis that the P/E ratio variances between the two companies are significantly different.
option_b: reject the null hypothesis that the P/E ratio variances between the two companies are significantly different.
option_c: reject the null hypothesis that the P/E ratio variances between the two companies are not significantly different.
explanation_en: The F-test is used to assess the equality of two population variances. Here, the comparison is between two companies' P/E ratios over a period of 20 years. The null hypothesis for the two-tailed test is that the variances are not significantly different, while the alternative hypothesis is that they are significantly different. Because the calculated F-statistic is higher than the critical F-statistic value, the null hypothesis will be rejected.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Quantitative Method\Reading 8 Hypothesis Testing - Answers.pdf
question_en: John Jenkins, CFA, is performing a study on the behavior of the mean P/E ratio for a sample of small-cap companies. Which of the following statements is most accurate?
option_a: A Type I error represents the failure to reject the null hypothesis when it is, in fact, false.
option_b: One minus the confidence level of the test represents the probability of making a Type II error.
option_c: The significance level of the test represents the probability of making a Type I error.
explanation_en: A Type I error is the rejection of the null when the null is actually true. The significance level of the test (alpha) (which is one minus the confidence level) is the probability of making a Type I error. A Type II error is the failure to reject the null when it is actually false.

question_en: For a two-tailed test of hypothesis involving a z-distributed test statistic and a 5% level of significance, a calculated z-statistic of 1.5 indicates that:
option_a: the null hypothesis cannot be rejected.
explanation_en: For a two-tailed test at a 5% level of significance the calculated z-statistic would have to be greater than the critical z value of 1.96 for the null hypothesis to be rejected.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Quantitative Method\Reading 8 Hypothesis Testing - Answers.pdf
question_en: A researcher is testing whether the average age of employees in a large firm is statistically different from 35 years (either above or below). A sample is drawn of 250 employees and the researcher determines that the appropriate critical value for the test statistic is 1.96. The value of the computed test statistic is 4.35. Given this information, which of the following statements is least accurate? The test:
option_a: indicates that the researcher will reject the null hypothesis.
option_c: indicates that the researcher is 95% confident that the average employee age is different than 35 years.
explanation_en: This test has a significance level of 5%. The relationship between confidence and significance is: significance level = 1 – confidence level. We know that the significance level is 5% because the sample size is large and the critical value of the test statistic is 1.96 (2.5% of probability is in both the upper and lower tails).

question_en: For a test of independence based on contingency table data, the test statistic is calculated as the:
option_a: mean absolute deviation of all table cells’ actual values and their expected values, if the two characteristics are independent.
option_b: sum of differences between each table cell’s actual value and its expected value, if the two characteristics are independent.
option_c: sum of squared differences between each table cell’s actual value and its expected value, if the two characteristics are independent.
explanation_en: The chi-square statistic for a test of independence based on contingency table data is the sum of squared differences between each table cell's actual value and its expected value, if the two characteristics are independent.

explanation_en: The test statistic for a hypothesis test concerning population correlation follows a t- distribution with n − 2 degrees of freedom. option_a: sum of the number of rows and the number of columns.
option_b: product of the number of rows minus one and the number of columns, minus one.

explanation_en: Degrees of freedom for a test for independence are [(r – 1) (c – 1)], where r and c are the number of rows and the number of columns in the contingency table.

| 16 | 1.337 | 1.746 | 2.120 | 2.583 | 2.921 | 4.015 |
| 17 | 1.333 | 1.740 | 2.110 | 2.567 | 2.898 | 3.965 |
| 18 | 1.330 | 1.734 | 2.101 | 2.552 | 2.878 | 3.922 |
| 19 | 1.328 | 1.729 | 2.093 | 2.539 | 2.861 | 3.883 |
| 20 | 1.325 | 1.725 | 2.086 | 2.528 | 2.845 | 3.850 |

Based on a sample correlation coefficient of −0.525 from a sample size of 19, an analyst −0.525√19−2 calculates a t-statistic of = −2.5433. The analyst can reject the √ 2 1−(−0.525) hypothesis that the population correlation coefficient equals zero:
option_a: at a 2% signicance level, but not at a 1% signicance level.
option_c: at a 5% signicance level, but not at a 2% signicance level.
explanation_en: With 19 − 2 = 17 degrees of freedom, the critical values are plus-or-minus 2.110 at a 5% significance level, 2.567 at a 2% significance level, and 2.898 at a 1% significance level. Because the t-statistic of −2.5433 is less than −2.110, the hypothesis can be rejected at a 5% significance level. Because the t-statistic is greater than −2.567, the hypothesis cannot be rejected at a 2% significance level (or any smaller significance level).

question_en: Robert Miguel, CFA, is a portfolio manager. On Saturday, one of his clients invited Miguel and his wife to be his guests at his luxury suite for a major league baseball playoff game, which they did. Miguel told his supervisor on Monday that they had attended the game with the client and that the suite was luxurious. Miguel has:
option_b: violated the Standards because disclosure must be in writing.
option_c: violated the Standards because he must disclose the gift prior to accepting.
explanation_en: In this case, Miguel has not violated the standards. For a gift from a client in appreciation of past service or performance, informing his supervisor verbally is sufficient. Standard I(B) Independence and Objectivity requires disclosure prior to accepting the gift "when possible," but in cases such as this when there is short notice, notification afterward is permitted.

question_en: Which of the following statements about the CFA Institute's Professional Conduct Program (PCP) is least accurate?
option_a: Possible sanctions include condemnation by a member’s peers or suspension of a candidate’s participation in the CFA Program.
option_b: If the PCP staff determine that a sanction against a member is warranted, the member must either accept the sanction or lose the right to use the CFA designation.
option_c: Members who cooperate with a PCP inquiry by providing confidential client information to PCP staff are not in violation of Standard III(E) Preservation of Confidentiality.
explanation_en: Members can accept or reject a disciplinary sanction proposed by the Professional Conduct Program staff. If the member rejects the sanction, the matter is referred to a hearing before a disciplinary review panel of CFA Institute members. The other statements are accurate.

question_en: At his golf club on Saturday morning, Paul Corwin, CFA, sees Frank Roberts, a friend and institutional client of his, who tells him that he is planning to sell his house on the 7th fairway. While golfing that day, Corwin tells Robert Lowe, a realtor, that Roberts is planning to sell his house and may need a realtor. He also tells Lowe that he manages an equities account for Roberts. If Corwin has not received permission from Roberts, he has violated the Standard on preservation of confidentiality:
option_a: both by disclosing Roberts’ plan to sell his home and that he is a client.
option_b: by disclosing Roberts’ plan to sell his home but not by mentioning that he was a client.
option_c: by disclosing that Roberts is a client of his but not by mentioning Roberts’ plan to sell his home.
explanation_en: Corwin violated Standard III(E) Preservation of Confidentiality by revealing his business relationship with Roberts without permission. Because the information that Roberts' plans to sell his home is not received as part of his professional relationship with Roberts, it is not covered by the Standard.

question_en: Doug Watson, CFA, serves in a sales position at Sommerset Brokerage, a registered investment adviser. Watson frequently drinks excessively. On one occasion, Watson was cited by local police for misdemeanor public intoxication. According to the Standard on knowledge of the law and the Standard on misconduct, Watson is in violation of:
explanation_en: Watson's excessive drinking is unfortunate, but we have no evidence that it has affected his work, professional integrity, judgment, or reputation. If he commits an act involving fraud or dishonesty, he would violate the Standard on misconduct.

option_a: use and pay for commercial transportation, if available.
option_b: obtain written permission from his employer before he accepts this invitation.

explanation_en: The recommended procedures for compliance with Standard I(B) Independence and Objectivity include the recommendation that analysts on company visits pay their own travel expenses and use commercial transportation if it is available.

question_en: Which of the following is least likely included in the CFA Institute Code of Ethics? Members of CFA Institute must:
option_a: place their clients’ interests before their employer’s interests.
option_b: strive to maintain and improve the competence of others in the profession.
option_c: use reasonable care and exercise independent professional judgment.

question_en: Dudley Thompson is a bond salesman for a small broker/dealer in London. His firm is the lead underwriter on a new junk bond issue for Ibex Corporation, and Thompson has sent details of the offering to clients. Thompson calls only his accounts over £1,000,000 for whom he thinks the issue is suitable. Thompson also posts his firm's optimistic projections for Ibex's performance in several Internet chat rooms. According to the Standards concerning market manipulation and fair dealing, Thompson is in violation of:
explanation_en: Thompson has not violated Standard II(B) Market Manipulation by posting his firm's projections for Ibex. A firm's recommendation of a security may increase its price without any intent to mislead the market. The firm has disseminated the details of the offering to its clients fairly, so Thompson may call individual clients without violating the Standard III(B) Fair Dealing.

question_en: In formulating her report on GammaCorp's common stock, Barb Kramer, CFA, did a complex series of statistical tests on the company's past sales and earnings. Based on this statistical study, Kramer stated in her report that, "GammaCorp's earnings growth for the next five years will average 15% per year." Her conclusion was based in part on a regression analysis with a high level of statistical significance. Has Kramer violated the Standard on communication with clients and prospective clients?
option_a: Yes, because she didn’t give complete details of the statistical model used.
option_b: Yes, because she failed to indicate that 15% growth is an estimate.
option_c: No, because her projections are within the generally accepted bounds of statistical accuracy.
explanation_en: Kramer violated Standard V(B) Communication with Clients and Prospective Clients. The problem is with the word "will." Kramer should have used "is estimated to be" to separate fact from opinion. Statistical estimates of future events are subject to change and should not be presented as certainties. She need not give complete details of the statistical model but should indicate its general characteristics and the important factors involved in her projections.
